title: Strict henselization as a limit
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$, and $x\in X$
a point with $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)=a>0$; put
$d=\kundim_xX$ and $X'=\Spec\bigl(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,x}\bigr)$,
the strict henselization of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit].
Then there is a separably closed field $L\supseteq K$
([def-kun-separably-closed]) and a presentation

$$
X'=\varprojlim_iX_i
$$

of $X'$ as an inverse limit of affine schemes $X_i$ of finite type over
$L$ with affine transition morphisms and
$\kundim X_i<\kundim X$ for every $i$.
(*Source:* the case of Stacks Project,
[Tag `0F0U`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0U) that is
used in this chapter, namely the presentation of the strict henselization as a
limit of smaller-dimensional finite type models. In the Stacks Project the
proof uses Noether normalization, Algebra, Lemma 10.115.5,
[Tag `00OZ`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OZ)
(available in this manuscript as thm:zl-relative-noether), a finite endomorphism of affine space putting the image of $x$ at the generic point of the
linear subspace, the description of the strict henselization as the filtered
colimit of the pointed etale neighbourhoods
([def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]), and the dimension bound for
an algebra which is quasi-finite over a polynomial ring.)

proof.text: Apply lem-kun-strict-local-algebraic-residue-models. The exposed compatibility equation for the structural maps p_i makes the same underlying scheme diagram a diagram over Spec L. Since I is cofiltered, Over.forget U preserves this limit. Keep the original strict-localization isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, compatible-model footnote; Tag 0B1C, dimension of an irreducible closed subset; residue-tower and chain argument

proof.text: For any model point v with image u, give kappa(v) its K-algebra structure via the composite to Spec K. Functoriality of residueFieldAlgebraMap gives the compatible K-kappa(u)-kappa(v) tower. Characterizing base-field maps on spectra and the K-morphism equation give the compatible K-L-kappa(v) tower. The first tower has algebraic last extension, so transcendence-degree additivity in the two towers gives trdeg_K L + trdeg_L kappa(v) = trdeg_K kappa(u). Apply the closed-irreducible dimension theorem to the two point closures, obtaining natural dimensions d,e and the same two residue transcendence degrees. Positivity of trdeg_K L gives d+1 <= e by cardinal arithmetic. Subspace monotonicity gives e <= dim U <= dim X.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, compatible-model footnote; Tag 0B1C, dimension of an irreducible closed subset; residue-tower and chain argument

proof.text: The point underlying the given geometric point supplies an irreducible closed subset of X, so dim X is not bottom. Finite type makes dim X a natural number N. If a model had dimension at least N, the generic end of a chain of length N would have point closure of dimension d >= N (the existing exists_le_topologicalKrullDim_closure_singleton lemma). Step 2 gives d+1 <= e <= N, contradiction. Combine this strict dimension bound for every model with the diagram and limit of step 1.
